name: maps
description: Map utilities (merge with resolvers, invert, filter and map keys and values, counters, multimaps, diffs) and dynamic JSON values with paths, pointers and merge patches

api.name: from_pairs
api.sig: fn from_pairs[K, V](pairs: List[(K, V)]) -> Map[K, V]
api.doc: The map of `pairs`; a later pair for a key replaces an earlier one, as in a series of `put`s.

api.name: from_pairs_with
api.sig: fn from_pairs_with[K, V, e](pairs: List[(K, V)], resolve: (K, V, V) -> V ! e) -> Map[K, V] ! e
api.doc: The map of `pairs`, combining the values of a repeated key with `resolve(key, existing, incoming)`.

api.name: from_keys
api.sig: fn from_keys[K, V, e](keys: List[K], f: K -> V ! e) -> Map[K, V] ! e
api.doc: The map from each of `keys` to `f(key)`.

api.name: from_lists
api.sig: fn from_lists[K, V](keys: List[K], values: List[V]) -> Map[K, V]
api.doc:
The map from `keys[i]` to `values[i]`; extra keys or values are ignored, and a repeated key takes
its last value.

api.name: index_by
api.sig: fn index_by[T, K, e](xs: List[T], key: T -> K ! e) -> Map[K, T] ! e
api.doc: The map from `key(x)` to `x` for each element; a later element with the same key wins.

api.name: group_into
api.sig: fn group_into[T, K, e](xs: List[T], key: T -> K ! e) -> Map[K, List[T]] ! e
api.doc: The elements of `xs` grouped by `key(x)`, each group in the order of `xs`.

api.name: to_hash
api.sig: fn to_hash[K, V](m: Map[K, V]) -> HashMap[K, V]
api.doc: The same entries as a `HashMap`.

api.name: from_hash
api.sig: fn from_hash[K, V](h: HashMap[K, V]) -> Map[K, V]
api.doc: The same entries as an ordered `Map`.

api.name: get_or
api.sig: fn get_or[K, V](m: Map[K, V], k: K, default: V) -> V
api.doc: The value for `k`, or `default` when `k` is missing.

api.name: is_empty_map
api.sig: fn is_empty_map[K, V](m: Map[K, V]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `m` has no entries.

api.name: find_key
api.sig: fn find_key[K, V](m: Map[K, V], v: V) -> Opt[K]
api.doc: The smallest key whose value equals `v`.

api.name: find_entry
api.sig: fn find_entry[K, V, e](m: Map[K, V], f: (K, V) -> Bool ! e) -> Opt[(K, V)] ! e
api.doc: The first entry, in key order, for which `f(key, value)` holds.

api.name: keys_where
api.sig: fn keys_where[K, V, e](m: Map[K, V], f: V -> Bool ! e) -> List[K] ! e
api.doc: The keys, in order, whose value satisfies `f`.

api.name: has_all
api.sig: fn has_all[K, V](m: Map[K, V], ks: List[K]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether every key of `ks` is in `m`.

api.name: has_any
api.sig: fn has_any[K, V](m: Map[K, V], ks: List[K]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether some key of `ks` is in `m`.

api.name: min_by_value
api.sig: fn min_by_value[K, V: Ord](m: Map[K, V]) -> Opt[(K, V)]
api.doc: The entry with the smallest value (the smallest key among equal values).

api.name: max_by_value
api.sig: fn max_by_value[K, V: Ord](m: Map[K, V]) -> Opt[(K, V)]
api.doc: The entry with the largest value (the smallest key among equal values).

api.name: merge
api.sig: fn merge[K, V](a: Map[K, V], b: Map[K, V]) -> Map[K, V]
api.doc: The entries of both maps; for a key in both, the value from `b` wins (like Python's `a | b`).

api.name: merge_prefer_left
api.sig: fn merge_prefer_left[K, V](a: Map[K, V], b: Map[K, V]) -> Map[K, V]
api.doc: The entries of both maps; for a key in both, the value from `a` wins (lodash `defaults`).

api.name: merge_with
api.sig: fn merge_with[K, V, e](a: Map[K, V], b: Map[K, V], resolve: (K, V, V) -> V ! e) -> Map[K, V] ! e
api.doc: The entries of both maps; for a key in both, the value is `resolve(key, from_a, from_b)`.

api.name: merge_all
api.sig: fn merge_all[K, V](ms: List[Map[K, V]]) -> Map[K, V]
api.doc: The entries of all maps, later maps winning; the empty map for an empty list.

api.name: merge_all_with
api.sig: fn merge_all_with[K, V, e](ms: List[Map[K, V]], resolve: (K, V, V) -> V ! e) -> Map[K, V] ! e
api.doc: The entries of all maps, folding repeated keys from left to right with `resolve(key, acc, next)`.

api.name: intersect_keys
api.sig: fn intersect_keys[K, V, W](a: Map[K, V], b: Map[K, W]) -> Map[K, V]
api.doc: The entries of `a` whose key is also in `b`, with `a`'s values.

api.name: subtract_keys
api.sig: fn subtract_keys[K, V, W](a: Map[K, V], b: Map[K, W]) -> Map[K, V]
api.doc: The entries of `a` whose key is not in `b`.

api.name: invert
api.sig: fn invert[K, V](m: Map[K, V]) -> Map[V, K]
api.doc:
The map from each value to its key. When several keys share a value the largest key wins,
because entries are visited in key order and later ones replace earlier ones.

api.name: invert_with
api.sig: fn invert_with[K, V, e](m: Map[K, V], resolve: (V, K, K) -> K ! e) -> Map[V, K] ! e
api.doc:
The map from each value to its key, combining keys that share a value with
`resolve(value, existing_key, next_key)` (keys arrive in ascending order).

api.name: invert_multi
api.sig: fn invert_multi[K, V](m: Map[K, V]) -> Map[V, List[K]]
api.doc: The map from each value to all keys that have it, in ascending key order.

api.name: filter_keys
api.sig: fn filter_keys[K, V, e](m: Map[K, V], f: K -> Bool ! e) -> Map[K, V] ! e
api.doc: The entries whose key satisfies `f`.

api.name: filter_values
api.sig: fn filter_values[K, V, e](m: Map[K, V], f: V -> Bool ! e) -> Map[K, V] ! e
api.doc: The entries whose value satisfies `f`.

api.name: filter_entries
api.sig: fn filter_entries[K, V, e](m: Map[K, V], f: (K, V) -> Bool ! e) -> Map[K, V] ! e
api.doc: The entries for which `f(key, value)` holds.

api.name: partition_entries
api.sig: fn partition_entries[K, V, e](m: Map[K, V], f: (K, V) -> Bool ! e) -> (Map[K, V], Map[K, V]) ! e
api.doc: The entries that satisfy `f(key, value)` and the ones that don't.

api.name: map_values
api.sig: fn map_values[K, V, W, e](m: Map[K, V], f: V -> W ! e) -> Map[K, W] ! e
api.doc: Every value replaced by `f(value)`.

api.name: map_values_with_key
api.sig: fn map_values_with_key[K, V, W, e](m: Map[K, V], f: (K, V) -> W ! e) -> Map[K, W] ! e
api.doc: Every value replaced by `f(key, value)`.

api.name: map_keys
api.sig: fn map_keys[K, V, K2, e](m: Map[K, V], f: K -> K2 ! e) -> Map[K2, V] ! e
api.doc:
Every key replaced by `f(key)`. When two keys map to the same new key, the value of the larger
original key wins; use `map_keys_with` to choose.

api.name: map_keys_with
api.sig: fn map_keys_with[K, V, K2, e](m: Map[K, V], f: K -> K2 ! e, resolve: (K2, V, V) -> V ! e) -> Map[K2, V] ! e
api.doc:
Every key replaced by `f(key)`, combining colliding values with
`resolve(new_key, existing, incoming)` in ascending order of the original keys.

api.name: map_entries
api.sig: fn map_entries[K, V, K2, W, e](m: Map[K, V], f: (K, V) -> (K2, W) ! e) -> Map[K2, W] ! e
api.doc:
Every entry replaced by the pair `f(key, value)`; on a key collision the later entry, in the
original key order, wins.

api.name: filter_map_values
api.sig: fn filter_map_values[K, V, W, e](m: Map[K, V], f: (K, V) -> Opt[W] ! e) -> Map[K, W] ! e
api.doc: The entries for which `f(key, value)` gives `some(w)`, with the value `w`.

api.name: pick
api.sig: fn pick[K, V](m: Map[K, V], ks: List[K]) -> Map[K, V]
api.doc: Only the entries whose key is in `ks`.

api.name: omit
api.sig: fn omit[K, V](m: Map[K, V], ks: List[K]) -> Map[K, V]
api.doc: The entries whose key is not in `ks`.

api.name: rename_key
api.sig: fn rename_key[K, V](m: Map[K, V], from: K, to: K) -> Map[K, V]
api.doc:
The map with the entry of `from` moved to the key `to`, replacing any entry already at `to`.
Unchanged when `from` is missing or equal to `to`.

api.name: adjust
api.sig: fn adjust[K, V, e](m: Map[K, V], k: K, f: V -> V ! e) -> Map[K, V] ! e
api.doc: The value at `k` replaced by `f(value)`; unchanged when `k` is missing.

api.name: update
api.sig: fn update[K, V, e](m: Map[K, V], k: K, f: V -> Opt[V] ! e) -> Map[K, V] ! e
api.doc:
The value at `k` replaced by `f(value)`, or removed when `f` gives `none`; unchanged when `k` is
missing.

api.name: upsert
api.sig: fn upsert[K, V, e](m: Map[K, V], k: K, init: V, f: V -> V ! e) -> Map[K, V] ! e
api.doc: `f(value)` at `k` when `k` is present, else `init` (Java's `Map.merge`).

api.name: alter
api.sig: fn alter[K, V, e](m: Map[K, V], k: K, f: Opt[V] -> Opt[V] ! e) -> Map[K, V] ! e
api.doc:
The entry at `k` decided by `f(current)`: `some(v)` stores `v`, `none` removes it (Haskell's
`alter`, Java's `compute`).

api.name: put_if_absent
api.sig: fn put_if_absent[K, V](m: Map[K, V], k: K, v: V) -> Map[K, V]
api.doc: The map with `v` at `k` only when `k` is missing (Python's `setdefault`, without the read).

api.name: counter
api.sig: fn counter[T](xs: List[T]) -> Map[T, Int]
api.doc: How many times each element occurs.

api.name: increment
api.sig: fn increment[K](m: Map[K, Int], k: K, by: Int) -> Map[K, Int]
api.doc:
The count at `k` raised by `by` (which may be negative); a missing key counts as 0, and a key
whose count reaches 0 stays in the map.

api.name: add_counts
api.sig: fn add_counts[K](a: Map[K, Int], b: Map[K, Int]) -> Map[K, Int]
api.doc: The counts of both counters added key by key.

api.name: subtract_counts
api.sig: fn subtract_counts[K](a: Map[K, Int], b: Map[K, Int]) -> Map[K, Int]
api.doc:
The counts of `a` minus those of `b`, keeping only keys whose result is positive (Python's
`Counter - Counter`).

api.name: most_common
api.sig: fn most_common[K](m: Map[K, Int], n: Int where _ >= 0) -> List[(K, Int)]
api.doc:
The `n` entries with the highest counts, highest first; equal counts are in key order. Fewer
when the counter is smaller; `n` 0 gives `[]`.

api.name: least_common
api.sig: fn least_common[K](m: Map[K, Int], n: Int where _ >= 0) -> List[(K, Int)]
api.doc: The `n` entries with the lowest counts, lowest first; equal counts are in key order.

api.name: count_total
api.sig: fn count_total[K](m: Map[K, Int]) -> Int
api.doc: The sum of all counts.

api.name: multi_add
api.sig: fn multi_add[K, V](m: Map[K, List[V]], k: K, v: V) -> Map[K, List[V]]
api.doc: The multimap with `v` appended to the list at `k`.

api.name: multi_get
api.sig: fn multi_get[K, V](m: Map[K, List[V]], k: K) -> List[V]
api.doc: The values at `k`, `[]` when missing.

api.name: multi_remove
api.sig: fn multi_remove[K, V](m: Map[K, List[V]], k: K, v: V) -> Map[K, List[V]]
api.doc:
The multimap with every occurrence of `v` removed from the list at `k`; the key goes when its
list becomes empty.

api.name: multi_from_pairs
api.sig: fn multi_from_pairs[K, V](pairs: List[(K, V)]) -> Map[K, List[V]]
api.doc: The multimap of `pairs`, each key's values in the order given.

api.name: multi_pairs
api.sig: fn multi_pairs[K, V](m: Map[K, List[V]]) -> List[(K, V)]
api.doc: Every (key, value) pair of the multimap, in key order and then list order.

api.name: multi_size
api.sig: fn multi_size[K, V](m: Map[K, List[V]]) -> Int
api.doc: The number of values in the multimap, over all keys.

api.name: same_keys
api.sig: fn same_keys[K, V, W](a: Map[K, V], b: Map[K, W]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether both maps have exactly the same keys.

api.name: equal_by
api.sig: fn equal_by[K, V, W, e](a: Map[K, V], b: Map[K, W], eq: (V, W) -> Bool ! e) -> Bool ! e
api.doc: Whether both maps have the same keys and `eq` holds for the values at each key.

api.name: is_submap
api.sig: fn is_submap[K, V](a: Map[K, V], b: Map[K, V]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether every entry of `a` is also in `b` with an equal value.

api.name: MapDiff
api.sig: pub type MapDiff[K, V] = {added: Map[K, V], removed: Map[K, V], changed: Map[K, (V, V)]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
The difference between two maps: entries only in the new map, entries only in the old one,
and keys in both whose values differ, as `(old, new)`.

api.name: diff_maps
api.sig: fn diff_maps[K, V](old: Map[K, V], new_map: Map[K, V]) -> MapDiff[K, V]
api.doc: What changed from `old` to `new_map`.

api.name: diff_is_empty
api.sig: fn diff_is_empty[K, V](d: MapDiff[K, V]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether a diff has no changes.

api.name: apply_diff
api.sig: fn apply_diff[K, V](m: Map[K, V], d: MapDiff[K, V]) -> Map[K, V]
api.doc:
`m` with a diff applied: removed keys go, added and changed keys take their new values. So
`apply_diff(a, diff_maps(a, b)) == b`. Keys of `removed` and `changed` are applied whatever their
current value is.

api.name: JsonValue
api.sig: pub type JsonValue = JNull | JBool{b: Bool} | JInt{i: Int} | JNum{f: F64} | JBig{digits: Str} | JStr{s: Str} | JArr{elems: List[JsonValue]} | JObj{fields: Map[Str, JsonValue]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A JSON value. Integers that fit `Int` are `JInt`; numbers with a fraction or an exponent are
`JNum`; a number that fits neither (an integer beyond 64 bits, or a float that overflows) is
`JBig`, which keeps its exact text. Object keys are kept sorted (a `Map`), so objects compare
and print the same whatever order their keys were written in. The functions below recurse on
nesting and are tested to 4096 levels in both tiers.

api.name: JsonError
api.sig: pub type JsonError = {message: Str, offset: Int, line: Int, column: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
Where and why JSON text failed to parse: `offset` counts characters from 0, `line` and
`column` count from 1.

api.name: PathSeg
api.sig: pub type PathSeg = Key{key: Str} | At{pos: Int where _ >= 0} derive Eq, Ord, Show
api.doc: One step of a path: an object key, or an array position.

api.name: Change
api.sig: pub type Change = Added{path: List[PathSeg], value: JsonValue} | Removed{path: List[PathSeg], value: JsonValue} | Replaced{path: List[PathSeg], before: JsonValue, after: JsonValue} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A difference found by `diff_values`, at a path from the root.

api.name: default_max_depth
api.sig: fn default_max_depth() -> Int
api.doc: The deepest nesting of arrays and objects `parse_json` accepts.

api.name: obj
api.sig: fn obj(pairs: List[(Str, JsonValue)]) -> JsonValue
api.doc: An object from key-value pairs; a repeated key takes its last value.

api.name: kind_of
api.sig: fn kind_of(v: JsonValue) -> Str
api.doc:
The kind of a value: "null", "boolean", "number" (`JInt`, `JNum` and `JBig`), "string", "array"
or "object".

api.name: is_null
api.sig: fn is_null(v: JsonValue) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether the value is `null`.

api.name: as_bool
api.sig: fn as_bool(v: JsonValue) -> Opt[Bool]
api.doc: The boolean, if the value is one.

api.name: as_int
api.sig: fn as_int(v: JsonValue) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc: The integer, if the value is a `JInt`, or a `JNum` with no fraction within the `Int` range.

api.name: as_f64
api.sig: fn as_f64(v: JsonValue) -> Opt[F64]
api.doc:
The number as an `F64`, for any number; a `JBig` integer is rounded and an overflowing one is
`none`.

api.name: as_str
api.sig: fn as_str(v: JsonValue) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc: The string, if the value is one.

api.name: as_array
api.sig: fn as_array(v: JsonValue) -> Opt[List[JsonValue]]
api.doc: The elements, if the value is an array.

api.name: as_object
api.sig: fn as_object(v: JsonValue) -> Opt[Map[Str, JsonValue]]
api.doc: The fields, if the value is an object.

api.name: parse_json
api.sig: fn parse_json(text: Str) -> Res[JsonValue, JsonError]
api.doc:
The value of JSON text, strictly as RFC 8259 says: one value with optional whitespace around
it, no comments, no trailing commas, no single quotes, no leading zeros or `+`, no `NaN`, and
strings with valid escapes and no raw control characters; a `\u` escape of a lone surrogate is
an error. A repeated object key keeps its last value. Nesting deeper than
`default_max_depth()` is an error.

api.name: parse_json_depth
api.sig: fn parse_json_depth(text: Str, max_depth: Int where _ >= 0 and _ <= 4096) -> Res[JsonValue, JsonError]
api.doc:
`parse_json` with a nesting limit: arrays and objects may nest `max_depth` deep (0 allows only
scalars).

api.name: error_text
api.sig: fn error_text(e: JsonError) -> Str
api.doc: The error as one line: "line 1, column 5: expected ':' after an object key".

api.name: render
api.sig: fn render(v: JsonValue) -> Str
api.doc:
The value as compact JSON text: no spaces, object keys in sorted order, strings escaped as
RFC 8259 requires (`"`, `\`, and control characters; other characters are written as they
are). A `JNum` that is not finite is written `null`; a `JBig` is written as its text.

api.name: render_pretty
api.sig: fn render_pretty(v: JsonValue, indent: Int where _ >= 0 and _ <= 16) -> Str
api.doc:
The value as indented JSON text: one element or field per line, `indent` spaces per level,
`": "` after keys, and `[]` and `{}` for empty containers. `indent` 0 still breaks lines.

api.name: quote_json
api.sig: fn quote_json(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc: The string as a JSON string literal, with its quotes.

api.name: parse_path
api.sig: fn parse_path(path: Str) -> Res[List[PathSeg], Str]
api.doc:
The steps of a dotted path such as `a.b[0].c` or `users[2]["first name"]`: names separated by
dots, `[n]` for an array position, and `["..."]` (with `\"` and `\\` escapes) for a key that
has dots, brackets or quotes in it. `""` is the root (no steps). A name can't be empty
(`a..b` is an error) and a position can't be negative or have a leading zero.

api.name: path_text
api.sig: fn path_text(segs: List[PathSeg]) -> Str
api.doc:
A path as text that `parse_path` reads back: plain names joined with dots, `[n]` for
positions, and `["..."]` for empty keys and keys with `.`, `[`, `]` or `"`.

api.name: parse_pointer
api.sig: fn parse_pointer(ptr: Str) -> Res[List[PathSeg], Str]
api.doc:
The steps of an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer such as `/a/b/0`: `""` is the whole document, every other
pointer starts with `/`, and `~1` and `~0` in a step stand for `/` and `~`. Every step is a
`Key`; on an array a key that is a position (`0`, `12`, not `01`) indexes it, and `-` means the
end (for `set_in`).

api.name: pointer_text
api.sig: fn pointer_text(segs: List[PathSeg]) -> Str
api.doc: A path as an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer, escaping `~` as `~0` and `/` as `~1`.

api.name: get_in
api.sig: fn get_in(v: JsonValue, segs: List[PathSeg]) -> Opt[JsonValue]
api.doc:
The value at a path, or `none` when a step is missing. A `Key` step reads an object field, or
an array element when the key is a position; an `At` step reads only array elements.

api.name: has_in
api.sig: fn has_in(v: JsonValue, segs: List[PathSeg]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether there is a value at the path (a `null` there counts).

api.name: set_in
api.sig: fn set_in(v: JsonValue, segs: List[PathSeg], x: JsonValue) -> Res[JsonValue, Str]
api.doc:
The value with `x` stored at a path, or why it can't be. Missing objects along the way are
created (and a `null` is replaced by one), as an object for a `Key` step and an array for an
`At` step. On an array the position must be at most its length (the length, or the key `-`,
appends), so arrays never get holes. A step into a boolean, number or string, a key that is
not a position on an array, or an `At` step on an object is an error that names the path.

api.name: delete_in
api.sig: fn delete_in(v: JsonValue, segs: List[PathSeg]) -> JsonValue
api.doc:
The value without whatever is at a path: an object field is removed and an array element is
taken out (later elements move down). Unchanged when the path is missing or `segs` is empty.

api.name: update_in
api.sig: fn update_in[e](v: JsonValue, segs: List[PathSeg], f: JsonValue -> JsonValue ! e) -> JsonValue ! e
api.doc: The value with the value at a path replaced by `f(old)`; unchanged when the path is missing.

api.name: get_path
api.sig: fn get_path(v: JsonValue, path: Str) -> Opt[JsonValue]
api.doc: `get_in` with a dotted path; `none` also when the path doesn't parse.

api.name: has_path
api.sig: fn has_path(v: JsonValue, path: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: `has_in` with a dotted path; `false` also when the path doesn't parse.

api.name: set_path
api.sig: fn set_path(v: JsonValue, path: Str, x: JsonValue) -> Res[JsonValue, Str]
api.doc: `set_in` with a dotted path; a path that doesn't parse is an error too.

api.name: delete_path
api.sig: fn delete_path(v: JsonValue, path: Str) -> Res[JsonValue, Str]
api.doc: `delete_in` with a dotted path; a path that doesn't parse is an error.

api.name: get_pointer
api.sig: fn get_pointer(v: JsonValue, ptr: Str) -> Opt[JsonValue]
api.doc: `get_in` with a JSON Pointer; `none` also when the pointer doesn't parse.

api.name: has_pointer
api.sig: fn has_pointer(v: JsonValue, ptr: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: `has_in` with a JSON Pointer.

api.name: set_pointer
api.sig: fn set_pointer(v: JsonValue, ptr: Str, x: JsonValue) -> Res[JsonValue, Str]
api.doc: `set_in` with a JSON Pointer; `-` as an array step appends.

api.name: delete_pointer
api.sig: fn delete_pointer(v: JsonValue, ptr: Str) -> Res[JsonValue, Str]
api.doc: `delete_in` with a JSON Pointer.

api.name: deep_merge
api.sig: fn deep_merge(a: JsonValue, b: JsonValue) -> JsonValue
api.doc:
`b` merged into `a`: where both are objects their fields merge recursively, anywhere else
(arrays included) the value from `b` replaces the one from `a`.

api.name: merge_patch
api.sig: fn merge_patch(target: JsonValue, patch: JsonValue) -> JsonValue
api.doc:
`target` with an RFC 7386 JSON Merge Patch applied: an object patch sets each of its fields
recursively and removes the fields it sets to `null`; any other patch replaces the target.

api.name: make_merge_patch
api.sig: fn make_merge_patch(source: JsonValue, target: JsonValue) -> JsonValue
api.doc:
The RFC 7386 merge patch that turns `source` into `target`, so
`merge_patch(source, make_merge_patch(source, target)) == target` whenever `target` has no `null`
inside an object (merge patches can't set a field to `null`). Unchanged fields are left out;
arrays are replaced whole.

api.name: flatten_value
api.sig: fn flatten_value(v: JsonValue) -> Map[Str, JsonValue]
api.doc:
The leaves of a value keyed by their `path_text`: scalars, and empty arrays and objects (so
`unflatten_value` can restore them). A scalar or empty root is the single key `""`.

api.name: unflatten_value
api.sig: fn unflatten_value(m: Map[Str, JsonValue]) -> Res[JsonValue, Str]
api.doc:
The value whose leaves are `m`, the inverse of `flatten_value`: each key is parsed with
`parse_path` and set with `set_in`, in path order (an empty map gives an empty object).
Errors when a key doesn't parse, when two keys conflict (`a` and `a.b`), or when array
positions skip one.

api.name: diff_values
api.sig: fn diff_values(a: JsonValue, b: JsonValue) -> List[Change]
api.doc:
The differences from `a` to `b`, in path order: fields and trailing array elements only in `b`
are `Added`, only in `a` `Removed`, and other values that differ `Replaced` (a change of kind,
or of a scalar). Arrays are compared position by position, so an insertion shows as
replacements plus an addition. Equal values give `[]`.

api.name: apply_changes
api.sig: fn apply_changes(v: JsonValue, changes: List[Change]) -> Res[JsonValue, Str]
api.doc:
`v` with changes applied, as `diff_values` produces them: `Replaced` and `Added` in order, then
`Removed` from the last to the first so array positions stay valid. So
`apply_changes(a, diff_values(a, b)) == ok(b)`. Errors when a path can't be set.
